text:
sara: quick thread on continuous-batcher admission tradeoffs. we've seen small, frequent requests balloon p99 because everything competes in the same coalesce. idea: a per-box lightweight admission layer that enforces three outcomes: FASTPATH, WARMUP, BATCHER. keep it admission-only.
ollie: agree. admission-only keeps the scheduler simpler. what metrics do we need to decide? token_count, deadline_hint, recent_enq_rate, and kv_cache_score maybe.
diego: +1. also include a small per-tenant credit ledger so noisy tenants can't monopolize fastpath. credits refill on a sliding window.
sara: prototype policy (informal):
```
if tokens<=24 and deadline<=50ms and credits>0 -> FASTPATH
elif tokens<=256 and kv_cache_score>0.5 and credits>0 -> WARMUP
else -> BATCHER
```
ollie: how to measure kv_cache_score cheaply? maybe recent requests with long context that hit KV; use an EWMA of hits normalized by expected benefit. keep it approximate.
diego: ops concerns: if FASTPATH pools saturate, automatic downgrade to BATCHER and emit an alert. avoid offering an overloaded low-latency path.
ops-bot: alert: fastpath_util=82% on pool-f. consider scaling or throttling fastpath credits. (auto)
sara: rollout plan: sim-mode for 72h (emit "would_FASTPATH"/"would_WARMUP" metrics + annotated traces) while always executing BATCHER. then enable FASTPATH on 0.5% of boxes -> 8% ramp, watch p50/p95/p99 and KV hit-rate. use canary tenants and routing kill-switch.
ollie: need telemetry labels: admission_decision, admission_reason, tenant_class, box_id, sim_mode_flag. plus histograms: enqueue_to_start_per_path.
diego: interface: gate returns tuple {decision_enum, reason_tag, decision_id} but per agents.md we should keep header simple; in code use enum+string reason. persist decision_id to trace.
sara: testing: replay one week of traffic through sim-mode to estimate KV delta and tail impact. also microbench fastpath p99 with small payloads.
ollie: long-term: consider adaptive thresholds driven by short-term load signals (e.g., backpressure from batcher queue length) but start deterministic. deterministic is easier to audit and has clearer failure modes.
diego: config surface: global defaults + tenant-class overrides (free/paid/enterprise) + opt-in flag for a small list of enterprise SKUs. avoid per-tenant full config.
sara: doc the admission contract and include migration playbook: sim-mode, small canary, ramp, and rollback via router. i'll draft RFC with proto, metrics, and sim csvs.
ops-bot: note: scheduled job will collect sim-mode traces nightly for the RFC authors.
sara: thanks all — i'll have a draft by Wednesday EOD. :white_check_mark:
